tools_used: web fetch (wlf.org, tlblog.org, supremecourt.gov docket PDF)
helpful: The provisioned petition.txt and questions-presented.txt: the full petition text made the split and vehicle analysis possible without fetching the PDF.
The CourtListener MCP read_document path gave the full Fourth Circuit opinion and Tango Music in two calls, which is what let me judge how square the split is.
The sal-v4 band table with bracketed reached rates and n per Term made the pooled anchor a short computation.
gaps: The statpack has no cut conditioned on a call for a response, which is the single strongest signal on this docket and the one the salience band does not see; the size of my adjustment for it is judgment rather than a published figure.
fedcourts query has no topical filter, so it cannot surface prior diversity-jurisdiction petitions; a subject or statute filter on SCOTUS rows would have given real priors.

The docket's September 24 letter was provisioned only as a link; the pipeline fetches petition and BIO text but not letters or amicus briefs, so the amicus brief's content reached me only through WLF's own summary.
notes: Retrieval total: 2 corpus commands (1 real query), 4 MCP calls, 2 web searches, 3 web fetches, 1 local PDF extraction. No MCP errors this run.
